note: Input byte 0x40 selects a literal header with incremental indexing, causing the decoded name and value to be inserted into the dynamic table.
The input-controlled name length is decoded from the HPACK stream and contributes to the dynamic-table entry size.
The input-controlled value length is decoded from the HPACK stream and combines with nlen to form the insertion length.
The indexed literal header transfers the decoded name and value into hpack_dht_insert for dynamic-table storage.
After the dynamic table has wrapped, safe insertion into headroom requires the previous head to still be the front entry; otherwise headroom must not be used.
The zero-length indexed header satisfies the size comparison even when the table is wrapped, making the missing non-wrapped guard decisive on vulnerable code paths.
A corrupted dynamic-table address is used as the destination for copying an input-controlled header name, producing an invalid write when the table metadata has been miscomputed.
